outcome: The hidden old simulation counters are no longer redrawn on every simulation step; whole-page watchers now wake about 3 times less often during runs
owner_impact: Nothing changes on screen. The simulation panel you see is the React one; the older labels underneath (time, physics ticks, control updates, actual speed) are kept as a fallback view in case the React panel fails to load, and are hidden otherwise. They were still rewritten about 50 times a second while hidden, and every rewrite woke the page-wide watchers. They are now drawn only while visible, and redrawn at once if they become visible. The seed label is rewritten only when the seed changes. Measured over 10 seconds of running: 1,535 watcher wake-ups (18 ms) instead of 4,548 (47 ms). The release check now reads the numbers from the panel you actually see. Test now: optional. Run, pause, change speed and restart with a new seed; the counters, seed and speed should behave as before.

next.text: #569 continues: retire the remaining duplicate old views that nothing reads, one panel at a time, and unify event names. Nothing changes on screen.

technical_evidence: main.js: drawLegacyCounters() draws time, ticks and updates from the runtime model only while body lacks vlab-react-simulation-mounted, and a body-class observer redraws when that changes; the seed label and #canvas-empty are written only on change.
runtime-speed.js: the legacy actual-speed label follows the same rule; the model is always updated.
React panel exposes data-vlab-simulation-seed and data-vlab-simulation-target; browser-smoke.mjs reads the visible panel's values when mounted, the legacy labels otherwise.
Fallback proof on the production build with the React bundle blocked: legacy counters advance (0 to 59.66 s, 20.0x) exactly as on main.

Full-page A/B, main versus this build: results, editor and extended apply scenarios byte-identical; simulation identical except the pause-time counters, which vary by about 3 s between runs of the same build (six runs, one fingerprint once masked).
Style comparison identical at all four viewports; 687 tests pass; typecheck clean.
